questions.q: In the SageMaker Model Registry, what does a model version actually store?
options: The trained model weights themselves, copied into the registry
A pointer to the container image and the model.tar.gz in S3, plus metadata such as approval status
Only the training dataset that produced the model
Only the endpoint configuration used to serve the model
questions.explain: A version records what is needed to run the model again (image, S3 model artifact, accepted content types, optional metrics and metadata). It points to the artifact rather than holding it.

questions.q: Which set lists the valid ModelApprovalStatus values described in the AWS docs?
options: Draft, Staging, Production
Pending, Live, Retired
PendingManualApproval, Approved, Rejected
Created, Approved, Superseded
questions.explain: The service uses PendingManualApproval, Approved and Rejected. 'Superseded' was only a label in the lesson's local sketch.

questions.q: With a SageMaker-provided MLOps project template, what happens when a version moves from PendingManualApproval to Approved?
options: Nothing; the status is purely decorative
The model version is deleted
CI/CD deployment of that version can be initiated
The model is automatically retrained
questions.explain: Per the docs, PendingManualApproval to Approved initiates CI/CD deployment for the approved version when you use the provided project templates. Moving to Rejected takes no action.

questions.q: What did the offline Stubber check in this lesson prove?
options: That AWS will accept the request values and create the resources
That the IAM role has permission to register models
That the request parameter names and structure match boto3's service model
That the model will score well in production
questions.explain: The Stubber validates the shape of requests against the local service model. It cannot prove permissions, valid ARNs or that the service will accept the values.

questions.q: Why encode the promotion rule (for example AUC of at least 0.75 and better than the current version) in code?
options: Because the registry refuses to accept versions without a rule
So promotion is repeatable and auditable instead of depending on someone's memory
Because boto3 requires a metric threshold on every call
To avoid ever needing a human reviewer for any model
questions.explain: A rule in code is repeatable and reviewable. The threshold itself is a project choice, not an AWS requirement.
